_comment: Expectations run by src/quality/run_gx.py. Same shape the Data Quality Agent proposes (proposals/quality_agent_expectations.json); a human merges accepted ones here. severity: critical blocks gold, warning is recorded, info is baseline measurement only.

bronze_baseline.why: An empty landing table means the extract failed upstream, not that there is no data.
ticket_id is the business key; rows without one cannot be deduplicated or joined, so they go to the DLQ.
Repeated keys mean double counting in every aggregate unless collapsed.
A ticket with no readable creation time cannot be placed on any timeline.
Measures format chaos: seven date formats in one column means naive casting silently corrupts or drops rows.
resolved_at may be blank (still open) but must otherwise be a real date.
Priority drives SLA and escalation reporting; 22 spellings fragment every GROUP BY.
Status decides what counts as open backlog; junk values make tickets vanish from it.
115 raw spellings (plus rows where category and description are swapped) make per-category reporting meaningless.
Placeholder buildings pollute location rollups with a fake site.
Non-person submitters indicate test or system-generated rows.
Currency symbols, N/A, TBD and negative sentinels break SUM/AVG, or worse, are summed as real money.
Only five SLA tiers exist in the data; 0, -1 and 999 are sentinels that would corrupt breach-rate math.

silver_gate.why: Publishing gold from an empty silver would silently wipe every dashboard.
Duplicate keys would double count in gold.
Anything else should have been routed to the DLQ.
Every aggregate in gold is time-based.
Normalization must leave only canonical values (NULL allowed).
Backlog logic depends on exactly these states.
A new canonical category must be reviewed here before it reaches gold.
Negative costs are sentinels and must be nulled before they are summed.
SLA of 0 or 999 hours would make every breach-rate meaningless.
Source defect: resolution before creation. Kept and flagged; gold excludes these from timing metrics.
Missing priority hides tickets from priority-based SLA reporting.
